newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Jardine Fleming sees both fund outflow and inflow.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming sees both fund outflow and inflow.

text.p: Jardine Fleming Holdings Ltd's fund management arm was seeing an outflow of client funds following a recent trading scandal at the firm, but new money was also coming in, a company spokesman said on Monday.
"We have lost some of the accounts (but) we are gaining new equities, particularly from Japan," said the spokesman for Jardine Fleming Investment Management (JFIM).

But he declined to comment on a report in London's Financial News on Monday that the UK's Civil Aviation Authority pension fund withdrew two portfolios of 21.5 million sterling each from Jardine Fleming.
"It's really not appropriate to talk about the identity of particular clients," he said.

Jardine Fleming Holdings' newly appointed top executives told the South China Morning Post in London that JFIM had seen funds of US$50-100 million "walk out" and up to US$3 billion in assets out of US$21 billion under mangement were "vulnerable".
Large British pension funds, including the US$32.4 billion IBM United Kingdom Pension Trust, were known to be reconsidering mandates they had placed with JFIM, the paper said.
